This page shows relations between genome-level statistics. Two caveats apply to everything here.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Caveats
The regressions do not control for phylogeny: genomes of one lineage are not independent, so the p-values and R-squared values describe the sample, not an evolutionary relation. Because no multiple-testing correction is applied to the group tests, p-values from many tests should be read as unadjusted.
:::

## All genomes (not only representatives)

The scatter plots use all genomes in the genome table, not one per species. Closely related genomes can therefore dominate. The caption of each plot gives n.

```{python}
single("A01_busco_vs_genome_size", "BUSCO complete against genome size.", "all")
single("A02_busco_vs_n_genes", "BUSCO complete against gene number.", "all")
single("A03_busco_vs_n50", "BUSCO complete against N50.", "all")
single("A04_busco_vs_contigs", "BUSCO complete against contig count.", "all")
single("A05_busco_vs_gc", "BUSCO complete against GC.", "all")
single("A06_busco_vs_gene_density", "BUSCO complete against gene density.", "all")
single("A07_genes_vs_genome_size", "Gene number against genome size.", "all")
single("A08_intron_len_vs_gene_density", "Median intron length against gene density.", "all")
single("A09_gc_vs_genome_size", "GC against genome size.", "all")
single("A10_busco_dup_vs_genome_size", "BUSCO duplicated against genome size.", "all")
single("A11_busco_missing_vs_contigs", "BUSCO missing against contig count.", "all")
single("A12_n50_vs_n_genes", "N50 against gene number.", "all")
```

## Regressions by group

One representative genome per species. The regression table gives n, slope, R-squared and the scale used for each pair.

```{python}
fig("R01_size_vs_genes", "Genome size against gene number.", "70%")
fig("R02_density_vs_intron_len", "Gene density against intron length.", "70%")
fig("R03_size_vs_intergenic", "Genome size against intergenic distance.", "70%")
fig("R04_gc_vs_gene_density", "GC against gene density.", "70%")
```
